To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the concept of sustainable development is applicable to the space domain; (ii) the current focus on national concerns obscurs larger issues of international inequalities, lack of access to space, barriers to capacity-building and technology absorption, and market protectionism; and (iii) the dominant understanding of space sustainability coincides with the "Governance for global security" logic, which focuses more on the present space actors' needs.

the concept of space cooperation as governance for global security is a dominant understanding that focuses more on the present space actors' needs, and the analytical tools designed with cosmopolitan approaches to international law express forms of cooperation to enable all participants in space exploration and utilization.
the concept of sustainable development is a useful framework for the development of space law and policy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how space sustainability can be achieved by the international community in a manner that is both equitable and fair.
how the concept of space cooperation is understood, how this is related to the concept of sustainable development, and how this understanding can be improved.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the current space governance system is inadequate for the future of space exploration and use, and that the international space community should adopt the cosmopolitan approach as an alternative to the existing system.
a cosmopolitan approach to space law is the best way to achieve the goals of space sustainability and the freedom of outer space.
a cosmopolitan approach to space law would be the most appropriate way to ensure the freedom of outer space for future generations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the concept of space cooperation as "governance for global security" should be redefined in terms of "governance to enable space sustainability," and that this should be the focus of the international legal framework for space cooperation.
the concept of "sustainable development" in space should be understood as a "freedom of outer space," which includes both the freedom of access and use and the freedom to develop.
space sustainability is a global issue that requires global governance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible for the space community, both present and future, to develop a common understanding of the need for a global space order, which will be sustainable in the sense that it will enable the space community to meet their needs and accrue their benefits while simultaneously enabling the future space community to do the same.
the space domain is not a zero sum game and there is no need to compete for resources.
the concept of sustainable space development is not just a technical or engineering issue.
